phases.title: The foundations
phases.text: Work starts on 5 January 1933. The cable anchorages and the piers of the two towers rise out of the ground and the water.

moments.title: A trestle torn open
moments.text: In 1933 a freighter rams the trestle leading to the south tower site. Two months later a storm carries off more than half of it.

moments.title: A bathtub at sea
moments.text: Around the future south pier, a concrete fender is cast under water. Once pumped dry, this “bathtub” lets the pier be built in the dry.

phases.title: The two towers
phases.text: The north tower rises from 7 November 1933, the south tower in the first half of 1935. Each tops out 227 m above the water, 152 m above the roadway.

moments.title: A colour born of primer
moments.text: The steel arrives coated in red primer. Seeing it from the ferry, architect Irving Morrow argues for an orange that matches the hills and stands out against sea and sky.

phases.title: Spinning the cables
phases.text: From October 1935 to May 1936, the two main cables are spun in place, above the strait.

moments.title: 27,572 wires
moments.text: Each main cable is not delivered in one piece: it is spun wire by wire, until 27,572 are bundled together.

phases.title: The deck
phases.text: The deck is hung from the cables, section after section. Construction ends on 19 April 1937.

moments.title: Half Way to Hell
moments.text: A net strung under the work catches 19 falling workers. They found the “Half Way to Hell Club”.

moments.title: The net torn away
moments.text: In February 1937 a scaffold falls and tears through the net: ten workers die.

phases.title: Opening
phases.text: The bridge opens to pedestrians on 27 May 1937 and to cars the next day. Its 1,280 m span is then the longest in the world.
